title: For Educators
meta_description: SoS HS is a five-session, music-driven mental wellness program for high schools. Built on Social and Emotional Learning, ready to run, evaluated with NYU. Now accepting pilot partners for the 2026 to 2027 school year.
lead: SoS High School is a five-session mental wellness program built on the music students already listen to. Run by your staff or by us. Minimal prep, no extra staffing, not therapy. Accepting pilot partners for the 2026 to 2027 school year.

why_music: Schools want to support student mental health but have limited staff, crowded schedules, stigma around traditional outreach, and few options that fit the school day. Music is already how students regulate stress, explore identity, and connect. SoS HS helps them do it with intention. It feels more like a listening lab than a lecture.

tracks.title: SoS HS
tracks.summary: Five ready-to-run sessions for advisory, classroom, or after-school settings. Students build playlists for stress, mood, and motivation, look at how lyrics shape identity, and talk in listening labs.
tracks.audience: School counselors, SEL leads, advisory and health educators, and administrators.
spec: Five ready-to-run sessions: music, the brain, and emotion; mental health and intentional coping; identity and self-expression; social connection and belonging; resilience and the future self
Minimal prep, no additional staffing, adaptable to any school environment
Co-designed with educators and mental-health professionals; activity-based and student-centered
For students: stronger coping skills, mental-health literacy, social connection, and earlier awareness before challenges escalate
For the school: safer spaces for conversation, stronger peer relationships, a shared language around mental health
A clear handoff to local mental-health resources and 988

tracks.title: Artist Visit
tracks.summary: A single event where an artist performs, then co-facilitates small groups with a therapist about coping, identity, and connection. The format that proved the idea in 2023, and a good way to start.
tracks.audience: Schools that want one event rather than the full program.
spec: An artist-led session built around a mental-health theme
Live performance, then small-group discussion with a therapist
A connection to local mental-health professionals and pathways to care
Past artists include Erick the Architect, Pink Siifu, Cleo Reed, Bryndon Cook, deem spencer, and Maassai

proof.heading: What we've learned

stats.body: Our first programs, in two NYC public high schools, funded by MTV's Mental Health Action Day: artists performed, then co-facilitated small groups with therapists. Students who had refused traditional support opened up.
A principal told us a high-risk student who had rejected every counseling outreach said that about the program. For us, that was the whole thesis proven.
of high-school students felt persistently sad or hopeless in 2021, and 22% seriously considered suicide. Students are more likely to seek support at school than in a clinic.
stats.source: CDC Youth Risk Behavior Survey, 2011 to 2021

credibility: Now piloting in Washington, DC; early pilots show strong engagement, especially in group listening and discussion
Evaluated in partnership with NYU's Ripollés Lab (Music and Audio Research Lab)
Co-founded by a clinician who has worked with adolescents; clinicians and crisis experts on our board
Trusted by partners including the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline, Save The Music Foundation, Loveland Foundation, TikTok, SoundCloud, and the U.S. Department of Education

lead_magnet.title: Why music: the research
lead_magnet.body: A Sound Approach, our white paper co-authored with NYU researchers and the We Are All Music Foundation, brings together the neuroscience, music therapy, and psychology behind using music intentionally for wellbeing, especially among youth underserved by traditional care.

intake.heading: Bring SoS HS to your school
intake.body: Tell us about your school and whether you want the full program or an artist visit. We follow up personally.
